facts: Biriyani is not one single recipe. Regional styles like Hyderabadi, Kolkata, Ambur, Thalassery, and Dindigul vary in rice, spice balance, layering, and cooking method.
The dum technique matters as much as the masala. A sealed pot traps steam so the rice finishes cooking while absorbing aroma from meat, stock, herbs, and fried onions.
Some famous styles use basmati, but others rely on shorter aromatic grains such as seeraga samba or kaima, which change the texture and flavor dramatically.
Potato in biriyani is strongly associated with Kolkata style and is treated as a feature, not a filler.
A good biriyani is usually about contrast: soft rice, juicy meat or vegetables, caramelized onions, fresh herbs, acid from yogurt or lemon, and warm whole-spice aroma.
